text:
maria: Kicking off kubeadm cluster bring-up in ca-central2 for the new GPU fleet. Goal: 3 control-plane nodes + 6 gpu nodepool (A100), multi-az, network policies locked down. Posting quick runbook notes and blocking items.

tj: :eyes: copy. Any quota checks done for GPUs and regional IPs?

maria: I requested GPU quota bump yesterday, AWS case #14532. Waiting for approval but need plan-B: preemptible spot pools + smaller on-demand reserve.

sre-elena: Note: ca-central2 has 1-hour maintenance window overlap with our other regions. We should avoid large rolling during that window.

infra-ops: Quick checklist I'm running:
- kubeadm init bootstrap
- CNI weave calico? (we recommend calico for network policy)
- MTU verify for overlay (1500 vs 895)
- ENI IP quota check
- GPU driver daemonset

maria: Using calico with IP-in-IP disabled (we want ENI-based IPs). mtus set to 1500. kubeadm init command:

```
kubeadm init --control-plane-endpoint="api.ca-central2.redwood.internal:6443" \
  --pod-network-cidr=10.32.0.0/12 \
  --upload-certs
```

tj: For nodepool manifest (kubeadm + kubelet config):

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: NodePool
metadata:
  name: gpu-a100-spot
spec:
  replicas: 6
  machineType: gpu-a100-40g
  preemptible: true
  taints:
    - key: gpu
      value: dedicated
      effect: NoSchedule
```

sre-elena: FYI, we had a networking hiccup in ca-central2 last quarter where MTU mismatch broke kube-proxy healthcheck. Add a post-apply: `kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide` and `curl` health endpoint between nodes.

deploy-bot: [system] Provisioning job started: gpu-nodepool-setup-1788881234. Status: nodes requested -> pending

infra-ops: Seeing kubelet errors on new node:
```
Jun 12 12:03:02 node-1 kubelet[1234]: E06012 12:03:02 kubelet.go:123] Failed to start Kubelet: failed to configure cni: failed to setup network: cni config not found
```

maria: That usually means the CNI daemonset hasn't come up / image pull blocked. Check image pull secrets and node's IAM role for ECR access.

tj: Also check sysctl for required kernel params for GPUs (nvidia-modprobe etc). Daemonset logs:
```
nvidia-device-plugin 0/1 nodes are ready: 0 nodes are available
```

infra-ops: Found failure: our bootstrap template used `imagePullPolicy: Always` but nodes had no internet (private subnet). Need to mirror images to internal registry or allow access via NAT gateway.

sre-elena: Cost tradeoff decision: If we mirror images and use on-demand for initial warmup, we can then scale spot A100. Spot interruptions will cause GPU eviction churn — recommend graceful drain script with 15m buffer.

maria: Agreed. Also gating factor: regional GPU quota only 4 GPUs on-demand. We'll open follow-up with finance for reserved commit if customer needs guaranteed throughput.

oncall: I'll take handoff once CNI and image mirroring done. Tag me `@oncall` when ready for health checks. Also create a post-boot checklist ticket in JIRA: INFRA-CA-234

tj: Post-boot validation commands we run:
- kubectl get nodes -o wide
- kubectl get pods -n kube-system
- kubectl describe pod nvidia-device-plugin -n kube-system
- run sample inference job to validate GPU scheduling

deploy-bot: [system] Provisioning job update: nodes provisioned 4/6, 2 pending, status: awaiting kubelet registration

infra-ops: One of pending nodes stuck in NotReady due to networking:
```
Status: NotReady
Conditions:
  NetworkUnavailable True
  KubeletReady False
```

maria: Looks like missing route table association for the AZ's subnet. I just attached the route to the NAT IGW and re-associated the subnet.

infra-ops: Rebooted node, kubelet registered -> now Ready. GPU device plugin shows 4 devices total across nodes.

sre-elena: Run cost check: projected monthly for this pool if we keep 6 A100 spot avg price $3.2/hr -> ~$14k/month. With 50% spot savings vs reserved commit, we can lower but need guaranteed capacity for SLAs.

maria: For handoff: current state -> control plane healthy, 4/6 GPU nodes Ready (2 provisioning retry), CNI restored, images mirrored to internal registry, imagePullPolicy changed to IfNotPresent. Open items:
- GPU quota request follow-up
- final network policy rules to restrict egress to S3 and internal services
- create reserved IP allocation for loadbalancer

oncall: Taking handoff. I'll run the health script and mark cluster green in PagerDuty runbook. Ping me when the last 2 nodes join or if preemption spikes.

tj: Documenting the small gotcha: CA-central2's default LB type doesn't support IPv6 dualstack for our loadbalancer; we had to explicitly choose NLB with IPv4 for external inference endpoints.

maria: Thanks all. I updated the runbook in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/internal/infra/ca-central2-kubeadm-runbook (added commands, snippets, and cost estimates).

oncall: Confirmed final check at 1788881299: cluster green, creating handoff checklist item in #incidents for long-running followups. :white_check_mark:
